title: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs
content: Nvidia reportedly discontinues GeForce RTX 5090-series products leaving GB202 for data center and professional graphics boards. GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB rumored to become de-facto flagship from the green camp for a while.

title: Ukrainian drones strike largest data center in Russia, multiple parts of 1.4 million square foot campus knocked offline
content: Following a Ukrainian drone strike on a D.C. in Sasovo, Russia, a Yandex facility in Kaluga has suffered a similar fate with multiple modules completely out of service.

title: Phison posts record September revenue as AI tops half of sales
content: Phison Electronics reported record September consolidated revenue of NT$30.639 billion (US$959 million), up 8% from August and 370% from a year earlier. The Taiwanese storage chipmaker said AI-related applications accounted for more than 50% of total revenue, underscoring how demand is expanding across storage, computing, networking and AI infrastructure.

title: Trump awards science medal to Elon Musk, Jensen Huang
content: US President Donald Trump will award the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and several other tech leaders, with major figures from the industry set to gather again on October 8, local time. The honors highlight Trump's push to spotlight technology executives as his administration emphasizes US innovation leadership.

title: Huawei faces price reset as memory costs surge
content: Huawei consumer business group chairman Richard Yu said surging memory component costs have added more than US$200 to the hardware cost of each Huawei smartphone, putting fresh pressure on handset pricing as the broader memory market climbs rapidly.

title: Zhen Ding posts record September sales on mobile demand and AI applications
content: Zhen Ding Technology said September 2026 consolidated revenue reached NT$26.358 billion (US$825.13 million), up 36.13% year over year and 27.54% from August, setting a monthly record. The PCB maker said the result reflected strong orders from mobile communications products as well as continued growth in its server, optical module and IC substrate businesses.

title: TPCA Show 2026 to spotlight AI computing, Unimicron chair keynote
content: As explosive AI computing demand drives hardware architecture change, Taiwan Printed Circuit Association (TPCA) is set to open its annual flagship event, with the 21st International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT-IAAC 2026) kicking off on October 19, followed by the 27th TPCA Show 2026 from October 20 to 22.

title: Unified memory lifts AI PC ambitions as Chinese open models gain local-inference ground
content: The hardware boundary separating cloud-scale AI from local inference is becoming increasingly porous as PC vendors expand memory capacity and software platforms make larger open-weight models easier to run directly on devices.

title: Semco moves glass substrates to package-level testing
content: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco) has reportedly completed initial reliability testing of its 100mm glass substrates and moved to package-level verification using customer chips, marking progress toward commercializing next-generation packaging technology as AI accelerators grow larger and more complex. The development comes as the company expands its existing semiconductor substrate business while facing uncertainty over the commercialization timeline for glass substrates.

title: JNTC bets US$259 million on glass substrates ahead of 2028 ramp
content: South Korea's JNTC plans to invest KRW347 billion (approx. US$259 million) in glass substrate manufacturing as it reports a sharp reduction in copper-filling time for thick glass cores, potentially easing a major bottleneck in advanced semiconductor packaging. The investment comes as the company advances customer evaluations, although meaningful mass-production revenue is not expected until 2028.

title: SK Hynix sends memory chips into orbit for testing
content: SK Hynix's dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and Universal Flash Storage (UFS) products have reached orbit aboard a South Korean satellite that successfully established communication with the ground following the country's fifth Nuri rocket launch. The mission opens the way for in-orbit reliability testing as the memory maker explores potential opportunities in the space electronics market. No in-orbit test results for SK Hynix's memory products have been announced.

title: Advanced packaging leads Malaysia's push up the chip value chain as AI reshapes demand, says Yole analyst
content: Malaysia is moving from traditional semiconductor back-end manufacturing toward higher value-added work, with advanced packaging set to drive growth over the next two to three years, according to Nur Hilwani, Technology & Market Analyst, Semiconductor Equipment at France-based Yole Group. Talent, IP ownership and supply-chain gaps remain hurdles.

content: A Senate investigation on AI data centers question that costs and benefits that AI hyperscalers show when they apply for permits to put up their developments. The report says that these claims are misleading and that they don't show the real impact of these sites on the local economy.
